Below is a deep dive into why self play works for two-player zero-sum (2p0s) games like Go/Poker/Starcraft but is so much harder to use in "real world" domains. tl;dr: self play converges to minimax in 2p0s games, and minimax is really useful in those games.

Self play works so well in chess, go, and poker because those games are two-player zero-sum. That simplifies a lot of problems. The real world is messier, which is why we haven’t seen many successes from self play in LLMs yet.

author: polynoamial
text: Over the past several months, we made a lot of progress on general reasoning. This involved collecting, curating, and training on high-quality math data, which will also go into future models. In our IMO eval we did not use RAG or any tools.

author: polynoamial
text: When you work at a frontier lab, you usually know where frontier capabilities are months before anyone else. But this result is brand new, using recently developed techniques. It was a surprise even to many researchers at OpenAI. Today, everyone gets to see where the frontier is.

author: polynoamial
text: This was a small team effort led by @alexwei_. He took a research idea few believed in and used it to achieve a result fewer thought possible. This also wouldn’t be possible without years of research+engineering from many at @OpenAI and the wider AI community.

author: polynoamial
text: It’s worth reflecting on just how fast AI progress has been, especially in math. In 2024, AI labs were using grade school math (GSM8K) as an eval in their model releases. Since then, we’ve saturated the (high school) MATH benchmark, then AIME, and now are at IMO gold.

author: polynoamial
text: Also this model thinks for a *long* time. o1 thought for seconds. Deep Research for minutes. This one thinks for hours. Importantly, it’s also more efficient with its thinking. And there’s a lot of room to push the test-time compute and efficiency further. https://t.co/TpDLBN6Q4N

quoted.text: @OpenAI @rao2z @OpenAI's o1 thinks for seconds, but we aim for future versions to think for hours, days, even weeks. Inference costs will be higher, but what cost would you pay for a new cancer drug? For breakthrough batteries? For a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis? AI can be more than chatbots https://t.co/AtqjRTzNMN

author: polynoamial
text: So what’s different? We developed new techniques that make LLMs a lot better at hard-to-verify tasks. IMO problems were the perfect challenge for this: proofs are pages long and take experts hours to grade. Compare that to AIME, where answers are simply an integer from 0 to 999.

author: polynoamial
text: Typically for these AI results, like in Go/Dota/Poker/Diplomacy, researchers spend years making an AI that masters one narrow domain and does little else. But this isn’t an IMO-specific model. It’s a reasoning LLM that incorporates new experimental general-purpose techniques.

author: polynoamial
text: Today, we at @OpenAI achieved a milestone that many considered years away: gold medal-level performance on the 2025 IMO with a general reasoning LLM—under the same time limits as humans, without tools. As remarkable as that sounds, it’s even more significant than the headline 🧵

quoted.text: 1/N I’m excited to share that our latest @OpenAI experimental reasoning LLM has achieved a longstanding grand challenge in AI: gold medal-level performance on the world’s most prestigious math competition—the International Math Olympiad (IMO). https://t.co/SG3k6EknaC

text: This isn't quite true. Test-time compute helps when verification is easier than generation (e.g., sudoku), but if the task is "When was George Washington born?" and you don't know, no amount of thinking will get you to the correct answer. You're bottlenecked by verification.

author: polynoamial
text:
@chamath Hard disagree. The biggest lesson of AI over the past 5 years is that scaling compute is the most effective path to stronger AI. The DeepSeek results are compatible with that. It’s clear now that trend will continue.

You make a second closed vs open source point that’s unrelated

author: polynoamial
text: @emollick I don’t think that’s the correct interpretation. DeepSeek shows you can get very powerful AI models with relatively little compute. But I have no doubt that with even more compute it would be an even more powerful model.

author: polynoamial
text: It can be hard to “feel the AGI” until you see an AI surpass top humans in a domain you care deeply about. Competitive coders will feel it within a couple years. Paul is early but I think writers will feel it too. Everyone will have their Lee Sedol moment at a different time.

text: @dieaud91 Between the o1 announcement, o3 announcement, and various podcasts/talks I think we've said a lot. We believe o1 represents a new scaling paradigm and we're still early in scaling along that dimension.

author: polynoamial
text: Lots of vague AI hype on social media these days. There are good reasons to be optimistic about further progress, but plenty of unsolved research problems remain.
